wrong_text: All thermoforming polymer products sold in the UK and EU must be marked with a recycling code
problem: Recycling identification codes (RICs 1–7) are voluntary, not mandatory, in both the UK and EU. The BPF recommends them and the system is widely used in practice, but there is no legal requirement for manufacturers to mark products. A student writing 'products must carry a recycling code by law' in an exam would be stating an incorrect fact.
correction: Change to: 'Thermoforming polymer products are widely marked with a recycling identification code — the triangle of chasing arrows enclosing a number — to allow consumers and recyclers to sort materials correctly. Marking is recommended by industry bodies such as the BPF and is standard practice across the UK and EU, though not yet a universal legal requirement.'

field: content_html — n17 (Recycling Codes intro sentence) + key-fact box n31
wrong_text: All thermoforming polymer products sold in the UK and EU must be marked with a recycling code [n17] … Thermoforming polymers carry recycling codes 1–7 [n31]
problem: Code 7 ('Other') covers thermoforming polymers that do not fit codes 1–6 (ABS, acrylic, polycarbonate, nylon, multi-layer laminates) AND is also used for some non-thermoforming materials. The statement 'thermoforming polymers carry recycling codes 1–7' is directionally correct but slightly misleading: not all thermoforming polymers are assigned a specific code — many code-7 thermoforming polymers have no established kerbside recycling. The key inaccuracy remains the mandatory-marking claim (logged as HIGH above). The code-7 framing is acceptable GCSE simplification and does not need correction beyond the mandatory-marking fix.
correction: No separate correction needed beyond the mandatory-marking fix above. The code 1–7 explanation in n18–n24 is accurate.
